content_preview.title: Box2D Creator Erin Catto Releases Box3D, an Open-Source 3D Physics Engine With Roots in Half-Life: Alyx's Rubikon
content_preview.summary: Erin Catto, creator of the Box2D physics engine, has released Box3D v0.1.0, an MIT-licensed 3D physics engine for games that blends Box2D code with remnants of Rubikon-Lite, a hobby version of the Half-Life: Alyx physics engine, and already powers Facepunch's s&box.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Erin Catto, the developer of the Box2D physics engine, has released Box3D, an open-source 3D physics engine for games. "I'm happy to announce the release of Box3D, an open source 3D physics engine. It is now available on GitHub," Catto wrote in [an announcement on Box2D.org](https://box2d.org/posts/2026/06/announcing-box3d/) dated June 30, 2026. The project's v0.1.0 build, titled "Initial Release," was published the same day on [GitHub](https://github.com/erincatto/box3d/releases/ta...

editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four gzipped snapshots from disk (source-0 box2d.org announcement, source-1 GitHub README, source-2 GitHub v0.1.0 release, source-3 Phoronix). VERIFIED VERBATIM against source-0: 'I'm happy to announce the release of Box3D, an open source 3D physics engine. It is now available on GitHub.'; 'You can think of Box3D as a fork of Box2D, extended with many features needed for 3D games'; 'remains almost identical to Box2D'; 'the falling trees moved erratically, teleporting around the screen'; 'almost all the APIs, data structures, and algorithms'; 'Eventually my Rubikon-Lite fork transformed into Box3D'; 'Open source is not a business for me. I develop Box2D and Box3D because I love working on game physics'; 'needs more testing and more complete documentation'; 'probably using a CLA'; making physics engines 'since 2004'; Kintsugiyama since 2022 on Unreal 5.0; Epic added gyroscopic torques 'late 2024'; Dirk Gregorius / Rubikon in Half-Life: Alyx / Rubikon-Lite / Ragnarok in future Valve games; early adopters s&box (Facepunch), Esoterica (Bobby Anguelov), Glenn Fiedler's 1000-player space game. VERIFIED against source-1 README: 'Uses sokol to run with D3D11 on Windows, Metal on macOS, and OpenGL 4.5 on Linux' and 'Box3D uses SSE2 with WebAssembly'; core library no dependencies beyond C runtime plus libm; MIT license. VERIFIED against source-2 release: titled 'Initial Release', body states 'This is the initial release of Box3D. I consider this to be alpha software.' VERIFIED against source-3 Phoronix (verbatim): 'began development after having issues with the native physics built into the Unreal engine' and 'the new Box3D code is derived in part from "Rubikon-Lite" as an offshoot of the physics engine for Half-Life: Alyx' and uptake 'by a few games and game engines/platforms'; MIT license.
